newsitem.title: USA: Boeing credits net increase to higher sales.
newsitem.headline: Boeing credits net increase to higher sales.

text.p: Boeing Co said higher net earnings in the fourth quarter, excluding a charge for an employee stock plan, were principally due to higher sales partly offset by a much higher effective income tax rate.

Higher net operating earnings for the full year also benefited from settlement of defense and space contract issues, recognition of tax benefits, reduced research and development expense and increased interest income, the company said.
Boeing also said it has retired $545 million of short-term debt assumed in its acquisition of Rockwell International Corp's defense and space units, which closed on December 6.
Boeing said it continues to expect its planned merger with McDonnell Douglas Corp to be completed in the summer of 1997.
Boeing said the operating profit margin for its commercial aircraft division fell to 12.8 percent last year from 13.8 percent in 1995, largely due to a product mix that included more 777s.
The profit margin on the 777 is lower than average because tools are being amortized over the first 400 units of the twin-jet aircraft's production.

Operating profit in the defense and space segment fell to 5.9 percent from 6.6 percent mainly because of costs associated with the Sea Launch and civil tilt-rotor programs and increased research and development expenses.
The company expects 1997 research and development expenses to be comparable with 1995 and 1996 levels, excluding the impact of the McDonnell Douglas acquisition.
The company spent $1.2 billion on R&D last year and $1.27 billion in 1995.
The company ended the year with $5.3 billion in cash and short-term investments, compared with $5.6 billion as of September 30 and $3.7 billion at the end of 1995.
Boeing's contractual backlog rose to $87.7 billion, compared with $84.3 at the end of the third quarter and $72.3 billion at the end of 1995.
